source_review.notes: Reviewed the original cuckoo-filter and quotient-filter papers, the cuckoo-filter analysis, the authors' counting-quotient-filter publication record, and primary vector/adaptive quotient-filter papers. All six final destinations returned HTTP 200. Performance, space, and false-positive claims remain attributed to their stated designs and experimental settings.

evidence: Checked cuckoo-filter bucket count N, bucket capacity b, fingerprint width f, population n, load alpha, primary index i1, alternate index i2, displacement delta, and relocation limit L.
Checked quotient-filter fingerprint width p=q+r, quotient and remainder extraction, canonical slot, run, cluster, and metadata terminology.
Checked that soft fingerprint collisions, full-fingerprint collisions, and original-key identity are kept distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter uses idealized hash notation only where the associated probability or engineering claim states its assumptions.

evidence: Recomputed the executable cuckoo fixture load as 15/(8*2)=0.9375 and confirmed its deterministic insertion trace performs four relocations.
Recomputed the quotient fixture as 15 fingerprints partitioned into 10 quotient runs, hence five same-quotient soft collisions.
Recomputed 3686/4096=0.89990234375 for the load example.
Recomputed 0xB6D3=46803, quotient floor(46803/64)=731, remainder 19, and 731*64+19=46803.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Finite fixture counts and textbook arithmetic are exact; they are not a throughput or false-positive benchmark.

evidence: Verified alternate-index involution algebraically: i xor delta(f) xor delta(f)=i.
Verified quotient decomposition and reconstruction: h=(h div 2^r)2^r+(h mod 2^r).
Verified copy-on-write relocation preserves the published table when a bounded insertion path fails.
Verified that exact ownership is sufficient to authorize deletion while a filter-positive result alone is not.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Hash independence and distributional behavior are explicit model premises rather than universal facts.

evidence: Reviewed empty and full buckets, zero alternate delta, bounded-kick failure, rollback, stash exhaustion, high load, duplicate fingerprints, and adversarial concentration.
Reviewed quotient wraparound, run and cluster boundaries, metadata corruption, full-fingerprint collisions, deletion compaction, resizing, merging, and concurrent readers.
Reviewed unowned and repeated deletion, partial persistence, crash recovery, incompatible hash seeds or layouts, and rebuild/bypass behavior.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable model omits concurrency, persistence, stash policy, resizing, packed quotient metadata, corruption injection, and adversarial hash experiments.

evidence: Every cuckoo entry remains in one of the two buckets derived from its stored fingerprint; the exact model checks this after all insertions and deletion.
Alternate-bucket selection is involutive for every inserted fingerprint in the fixture.
Deletion of owned key 27 succeeds, unowned key 99 is rejected without mutation, and every remaining inserted key still returns positive.
Every quotient/remainder pair reconstructs its original eight-bit fingerprint; exact output checks all table, ownership, run, and validity fields.
invariant_checking.notes: The quotient portion models decomposition and ordered runs, not the packed metadata transitions of a production quotient filter.

evidence: Reviewed cuckoo membership soundness from two-candidate placement through bounded relocation and atomic publication.
Reviewed alternate-index reversibility from fingerprint-derived displacement and XOR involution.
Reviewed quotient-filter recoverability from canonical quotient ordering, remainder storage, run boundaries, and metadata invariants.
Reviewed deletion safety from exact ownership through precise fingerprint occurrence removal and postcondition validation.
proof_review.notes: No production concurrency proof, full packed quotient-filter proof, or cryptographic adversary guarantee is claimed.

evidence: Mechanism explanations, invariants, bounded model checks, empirical paper results, and operational recommendations are labeled separately.
The chapter explicitly limits the finite Python model and does not present execution as proof of asymptotic, probabilistic, concurrent, or persistent correctness.
Cuckoo and quotient filter similarities are connected without treating their placement and metadata mechanisms as interchangeable.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: All proof-shaped arguments state the representation and hash premises on which they depend.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact seventeen-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
Independent recomputation reproduced the load, relocation, quotient-run, collision, and split/reconstruction values.
All six final external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local Markdown, front-matter, link, and snippet checks passed before review.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production hash function, packed cuckoo or quotient implementation, randomized false-positive study, throughput benchmark, concurrency test, persistence fault test, or deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter distinguishes two-choice fingerprint placement from quotient-ordered compact hashing, centers representation invariants, and treats failed insertion and unsafe deletion as contract-visible outcomes.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed API semantics, hash and seed compatibility, kick limits, copy-on-write publication, stash and rebuild policy, ownership-gated deletion, quotient metadata, persistence, concurrency, metrics, fault injection, and upgrade/rollback evidence.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review contrasts both structures; the executable model makes placement and decomposition inspectable; ten examples cover involution, load, splitting, failure, deletion, clusters, merging, persistence, concurrency, and selection; five exercises provide matched derivations and designs.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Fan, Andersen, Kaminsky, Mitzenmacher, Eppstein, Bender, Pandey, Johnson, Patro, database, storage, concurrency, security, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production cuckoo filter, packed quotient or counting quotient filter, concrete false-positive rate, concurrent/persistent protocol, certification, nor deployment fitness.
